data.title: Search Results Shaped to Surface the Narrative
data.summary:
Search results for the organisation's name, brands or executives were manipulated so that
campaign content ranks alongside or above authoritative sources.
data.description:
Most people meet a controversy through search rather than through the platform where it
started. Shaping the result page therefore reaches an audience far larger than the
campaign's own following, and it reaches them at the moment they are deciding what to
think.

The techniques are ordinary search engine optimisation applied to hostile content:
keyword-matched pages, reciprocal linking between campaign properties, and content
published to high-authority domains that accept contributions. The campaign's own
infrastructure is frequently exposed by the link graph, which makes this a productive
avenue for mapping the network.

Result pages differ by location and personalisation, so record the conditions of
observation. A screenshot without them is not reproducible evidence.
data.recommendation:
* Record search results with the query, locale and date, and repeat on a schedule to
  evidence persistence.
* Ensure the organisation's own authoritative pages are well structured and current, since
  displacement is more achievable than removal.
* Use the link graph between ranking pages to map campaign infrastructure.
data.short_recommendation: Record ranked results with locale and date; strengthen authoritative pages.
